attrs.evidence: The syntactic theorem, at its own strength. Over all 21 pairs the intersection of {origin_refs ∪ assumption_refs ∪ common_cause_refs} is never empty, and the floor is ASM-SUBSTRATE-INTEGRITY. WHAT THIS IS FOR: it is a place to LOOK for common-cause failure, and a standing refutation of the idea that this artifact's gates are diverse readings. WHAT IT IS NOT: a claim that any two instruments fail together. Declared overlap is not common cause; common cause is not measured statistical dependence; and neither is established here. FAC-INDEP remains open and unmeasured, and the gate refuses `independent: true` AND `independent: false` as derived facts — R6 guarded only the optimistic polarity and the error GPT-5.6 caught was the pessimistic one.

coverage.domain: every unordered pair of the instruments registered in mosaic/evidence.json

attrs.prior_art: GPT-5.6's audit of INV-R6 §5. Knight & Leveson (IEEE TSE 1986) and Kohli (arXiv:2605.29800, 2026) for why disjointness fails in the other direction; the common-cause-failure literature for the distinction between shared cause and probabilistic dependence.
